solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Attractive source? More or less

parts.note: attractive means pretty
a well is a source of water

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a pretty spring counts as a source, and gets a shrug for an answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: 'pretty well done' means almost or approximately done, i.e. more or less.

clue.text: Bill in gym showing speed of movement

indicators.note: the bill sits within the letters for the gym

parts.note: PE, physical education, is school gym class
AC is short for account, a bill

explanation.surface: A gym bill reveals how fast someone has been moving on the treadmill.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a walker's or runner's rate of going is their pace.

clue.text: Bird near inlet regularly

indicators.note: regularly takes every other letter of the words near inlet, starting from the second

explanation.surface: A bird is spotted close to a coastal inlet, as it often is.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the sea eagle, a classic crossword bird, is one kind of bird.

clue.text: Gee! He won't bet! Unexpectedly novel

indicators.note: unexpectedly signals the letters of the exclamation coming out in a surprise order

explanation.surface: A surprised exclamation that some gambler is refusing to place a wager.
explanation.walkthrough: L. P. Hartley's 1953 novel, filmed in 1971, opens 'The past is a foreign country'.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: L. P. Hartley's book about a boy carrying lovers' messages is a novel.

clue.text: Forgo gesture, by sound of it

indicators.note: by sound of it says the word for gesture is heard, not spelt

parts.note: a wave is a hand gesture

explanation.surface: Someone gives up making a gesture, judging from what can be heard.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to waive a right or fee is to forgo it, give it up voluntarily.

clue.text: Learner on farm referring to a weather forecast maybe

definitions.text: referring to a weather forecast maybe

parts.note: L is the learner driver's plate
a grange is a farm with its buildings

explanation.surface: A trainee on a farm talks about what the weather will do.
explanation.definitionFit: A forecast covering weeks or months ahead is described as long-range, as opposed to short-term.

clue.text: Close, quiet, unlit, empty

parts.note: SH is the call for quiet

indicators.note: empty strips out the inside of unlit, keeping its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A list describing a house at night: near, silent, dark and deserted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Close' looks like an adjective (near) in a run of adjectives, but it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to close a door is to shut it.

clue.text: Defying convention, smuggling in millions, sealed

indicators.note: smuggling in means sneaking the abbreviation for millions inside

parts.note: heretical means going against accepted belief
M is the abbreviation for million(s)

explanation.surface: A rule-breaker brings in millions in a sealed container.
explanation.definitionFit: Variant of hermetic: airtight, as in a hermetically sealed jar.

clue.text: Revise term in contrived manner? He might

definitions.text: Revise term in contrived manner? He might

indicators.note: in contrived manner says the two words are put together artificially in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone fiddles a term's wording to suit themselves, and the clue asks who would.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: an opportunist who bends with the times might well revise terms artfully.
explanation.definitionFit: A timeserver adapts opinions to suit prevailing fashion or authority, so would twist wording expediently.

clue.text: Finish off religious building that is initially not thought suitable

indicators.note: finish off removes the final letter of the building

parts.note: a convent houses nuns
IE (id est) means that is

indicators.note: initially takes the first letters of not and thought

explanation.surface: A religious building is first judged unsuitable.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an arrangement that suits you, handy or fitting, is convenient.

clue.text: Concert for first of May

parts.note: pro means in favour of, for

indicators.note: first of takes the opening letter of May

explanation.surface: A concert is scheduled for the first of May.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a promenade concert, such as the BBC Proms in London's Royal Albert Hall.

clue.text: Unease about extremely reckless story raised in song

indicators.note: about places the word for unease around the other pieces

parts.note: malaise is a vague unease

indicators.note: extremely takes the end letters of reckless
raised turns the word for story upwards, reading it backwards in a down entry

parts.note: a lie is a made-up story

explanation.surface: Discomfort over a rash tale being told in a song.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'raised' turns the story upward; 'about' wraps the unease around both inner pieces, splitting it after its second letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the French national anthem is a song.

clue.text: Cracking guys back — see order after unravelling?

indicators.note: after unravelling says the words back, see and order are untangled into a new order

explanation.surface: Some splendid fellows return to inspect an instruction once it has been undone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cracking' looks like praise (excellent guys) but means breaking codes.
explanation.definitionFit: People who crack ciphers, like those at Bletchley Park, are men doing the cracking.

clue.text: Quarterly test including obscure terms

indicators.note: including means the test holds the other letters

parts.note: a trial is a test

indicators.note: obscure means the letters of terms are muddied into a new order

explanation.surface: A test held every three months includes some difficult vocabulary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'obscure' scrambles the five letters of terms, which 'including' then places within the test word, splitting it after its third letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Occurring every three months, i.e. once a quarter-year.

clue.text: Speaker I introduced to parent agreed postponement

indicators.note: introduced to puts the speaker and I inside the parent

parts.note: mum is a mother
an orator is a public speaker

explanation.surface: A speaker meets a parent and they settle on delaying something.
explanation.definitionFit: A formally agreed delay or suspension of activity, such as debt repayments.

clue.text: Former inhabitant of Africa — island fellow

parts.note: Rhodes is a Greek island
Ian is any man's name, a fellow

explanation.surface: Someone who once lived in Africa turns out to be an island man.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhodesia, now Zimbabwe, was a former African state, so its people are former inhabitants of Africa.

clue.text: Confidentially at home chatter about foursome

parts.note: in means at home

indicators.note: about puts the chatter around the foursome

parts.note: to prate is to chatter
IV is four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Four people gossip discreetly at home.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym phrase: something said privately, not in public, is said confidentially.

clue.text: One going downhill fast in winter?

definitions.text: One going downhill fast in winter?

parts.words: One going downhill fast in winter?
parts.note: sounds like someone in rapid decline, but means a sports person speeding down snowy slopes

explanation.definitionFit: Someone racing down a snowy mountain on two boards in winter sport is the person meant.

clue.text: Tom's cry maybe as ambition rebuffed — "That hurts!"

indicators.note: rebuffed means turned back, so the word for ambition is read backwards

parts.note: an aim is an ambition
ow is a cry of pain

explanation.surface: Someone yelps in pain as their ambition is turned down.
explanation.walkthrough: A tom is a male cat.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a cat's mewing sound is the cry of a tom.

clue.text: Imply some get a cider pack on way back

indicators.note: on way back reads the chosen letters backwards
some says only part of the words get a cider pack is used

explanation.surface: Someone suggests a few people should grab a pack of cider on the trip home.
explanation.definitionFit: Formal sense: to predicate something is to assert or imply it as a quality.

clue.text: Smutty communications?

parts.note: smutty looks like rude or obscene, but here means sooty, messages sent by puffs of fumes

explanation.definitionFit: Messages sent by puffs of sooty fumes over a fire, so literally smutty communications.

clue.text: Upset Aidan's girl

indicators.note: upset means the letters of Aidan are knocked into a different order

explanation.surface: Aidan's girlfriend is distressed.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a female first name, here standing for any girl.

clue.text: Hard to avoid temporary difficulty or seven-year one?

indicators.note: to avoid means the letter for hard is left out

parts.note: a hitch is a temporary snag
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A question of whether a snag is hard to dodge, or the seven-year kind.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'seven-year itch' is the supposed restlessness in a marriage after seven years.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: the seven-year one is the urge to stray said to strike couples after seven years.

clue.text: Bird reduced — a bargain

indicators.note: reduced means cut short, so the bird loses its last letter

parts.note: a snipe is a wading bird

explanation.surface: A bird in a sale is cut in price and becomes a good deal.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal British sense: something cheap at its price is a steal or bargain.

clue.text: Surprise visit of Gunners tracked by papers

indicators.note: tracked by means followed by, so the papers come after the gunners

parts.note: RA, the Royal Artillery, are the gunners of the British Army
ID means identity papers

explanation.surface: Artillerymen make an unexpected call, followed by reporters.
explanation.definitionFit: A sudden swoop by police or troops is an unannounced visit.

clue.text: Tailor the brand, it's tough and realistic

indicators.note: tailor means cut and reshape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Advice to adjust the brand, which is hard-wearing and practical.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone toughened by experience and unsentimental is described this way.

clue.text: Source of light circuit Mike's installed

indicators.note: installed means the letter for Mike is put inside the circuit

parts.note: a lap is one circuit of a track
Mike is M in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: An electrician named Mike fits a circuit that powers a light.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a lamp is a device that gives out light.

clue.text: Age — it helps — working in diplomatic post?

indicators.note: working means the letters are put to work in a new order

explanation.surface: Experience is useful when serving in a diplomatic posting.
explanation.definitionFit: The office held by a legate, a papal envoy, is a diplomatic position.
